Ask whoever decides it: the advisor what is technical and you cannot decide; the architect what is the project's (the item itself must change, the scope is too large for one work, the order of items, how it fits the plan, another item or project must deliver first, a root outside the work blocks it, the system lacks a tool, data, credentials or a permission); the owner what the owner wants of this work, when the item and the owner's words leave it open. A choice between reasonable designs is no question: it goes to deep research, which puts what stays uncertain to the owner as a decision point. Ask, and never work around it, when a merge conflict cannot be resolved or a field you are asked to return cannot sensibly be filled, never forcing a value into it. When the reply comes, you carry on. When several must be asked, ask one, and the next when the reply comes

tools.name: ci
tools.desc: Pushes your local commits and runs the repository's fast CI on the commit; where the project runs its CI on demand, it runs only what you name: the tests you list, and the checks you name. When it is done, it gives you the result of each check and of each test you listed, and puts in your worktree, uncommitted, the files a red run generated that differ from yours, such as the files as the formatter makes them. The full CI, every check and every test, runs once, at the merge
tools.runs: The engine checks the request and the head, telling everything wrong with them at once, and pushes. On the first push of a commit beyond main it opens a draft PR with the title and description handed in, and updates them when new ones come; GitHub opens none for a branch with no commit beyond main, so a push of such a branch opens none and only runs the fast CI. Where the project's configuration has its CI run on demand (on_demand), the push runs nothing: the engine runs the fast CI workflow the configuration names on the branch by hand with the tests listed, which runs those tests, each to its end, and the checks named, among those the configuration lists (named_checks), given by the input it names (checks_input), and it takes only the run it made, never one made before; a job the run skipped, as the lint when it is not named, is not among the checks it gives. When no test is listed and no check named, it runs nothing and gives no check. Otherwise the push runs the fast CI workflow, the whole of it, which stops a job at its first red test. GitHub runs a workflow by hand on a branch by the file of it the branch holds; where it refuses to, as on a branch made before main's workflow took the request, and main's CI files (.github/) differ from the branch's, the engine runs it on a temporary ref holding the head with main's CI files, those the work changed itself kept as the work has them, gives that run as the head's and deletes the ref. The engine waits for the run to finish and downloads the logs of red checks. When tests are listed, it downloads the results the run reported, JUnit XML in the artifact the configuration names (`project.ci.results`), and reads from them what became of each test each listed name names and how long it took; a test the run did not reach is not run. When the run is red and uploaded the artifact of generated files the configuration names (generated_artifact), such as the files as the formatter makes them, it writes those that differ from the worktree's into it

tools.name: ci_before
tools.desc: Runs the tests you list on the code before the change: the engine puts these tests' files on the code before the change, runs them, and gives you the result of each check and of each test. Nothing goes onto this work's branch. Only files in the test paths go there: a test written in a file of the implementation cannot, since that file's change is the change itself, so write it in a file of its own in the test paths. A test that cannot run on the code before the change, as one that needs what only the change adds to be built or to reach what it tests, is not run there: say so where you report the test, and why, and the review judges it
tools.runs: The engine takes the listed files from the pushed head, puts them on the commit this work's branch forked from main, and commits that to a temporary branch. Where the project's fast CI takes the tests to run (its configuration's tests_input), the engine runs that workflow on the branch with the listed tests, which runs exactly them, each to its end. Otherwise the push runs the whole fast CI, which stops a job at its first red test, where the project's configuration says its CI runs on those branches (runs_on_before_branches, true unless set); where it says it does not, nothing is pushed, and the tool refuses, saying so. Where GitHub refuses to run the workflow by hand with the CI files (.github/) of the code before the change, as those of a branch made before main's took the request, and main's differ, the engine puts main's CI files on that code and runs it again. It waits for the run to finish, downloads the logs of red checks, deletes the temporary branch, and reads what became of each test each listed name names from the results the run reported, JUnit XML in the artifact the configuration names (`project.ci.results`). A unit of tests that could not be built on the code before the change, as one that uses what the change adds, is reported as not built, and the tests of every other unit still run

steps.start_work: Has the session manager set up where the work runs and the engineer's session, on a machine with a free slot. An item worked on here before takes over its latest earlier work's branch, its worktree (reused when it is there, made afresh from the branch otherwise) and its PR; an item imported with a branch takes that branch and the PR imported with it; any other item gets a new branch from main.
steps.run_tools: Runs the tools the calling cell asked for, from the commits the session manager bundled. When the work comes back from the architect, it runs again only the tools that failed. A tool that fails is retried twice before it counts as failed.
steps.merge: Puts the PR in this repository's merge queue; at its turn, catches it up with main, runs the full CI once and merges it when it is green: the three one after another, the queue taking one work at a time. Where the project's CI runs on demand, the full CI on the head is a run made by hand now; the merge waits for a green run of the full CI, never for one of the fast CI, and a run without a check merging needs is red. A conflict or a red check goes back to the engineer, who fixes everything with the fast CI before the full CI runs again; the third time in a row it goes to the architect.
steps.ask_architect: Queues what is asked for the architect, starting a work of the architect when none runs; the engineer's work stops and waits without holding a slot. The architect answers with a reply, brought back unchanged. The split of a design along its parts (cell `D5`) is queued so too, as an engineer's question of its own kind.
steps.ask_owner: Puts what is asked before the owner, as an ask of the owner in the owner's interface, and notifies the owner. For the architect, the ask holds only the matter of the path that asked, and the architect's work goes on; the owner's chosen option or sentence goes back unchanged to the side that asked: for a held matter, when it is picked again, to the cell that asked. For an engineer's work, the work waits for the answer, holding no slot, and the answer goes back unchanged to the cell that asked: the engineer's question about what the owner wants, the owner's review of a design, or the owner's approval of a change.
steps.end_work: Ends the work as every work ends, and keeps its branch. A work whose whole item went to sub-items ends here without merging, and its item is done once the sub-items are merged.
steps.wait_for_matter: No work of the project's architect runs: the engine takes this cell's rows for each project whose architect runs none, without a round, and one that takes `due` gets a work of the architect's graph, on no item, which starts at the cell that row leads to. The work holds no slot, and one runs at a time for each project; once it ends, the project waits here again. What was said in the works' groups since the architect last read it is queued first (`queue_group_talk`).
steps.look_at_queue: Looks at the project's queue: which matters can be picked now (not parked by a question the owner has not replied to, due, flow feedback, its own or forwarded by another project's architect, and what was said in the works' groups only when it came before the architect's work started, and while new starts are held to set things straight, those that set them straight and those an agent stopped waiting for), and how many this batch handled. The owner's words are taken first, the oldest of them, then a matter back with the owner's reply, the oldest of them; then, when the newest question pending was put less than the wait for the owner's reply ago and the owner said nothing to the architect since, the architect waits for the reply (a question that pins an open question of an engineer's design is not waited for: that engineer's work goes on without its answer); then, when the architect answered the owner's words less than that wait ago and the owner said nothing since, it waits for the owner's next words; then a matter of two cells waiting for its second cell; then the matters at the head of the queue, the check of the policy before the plan of what to do next; and exactly one matter that can be picked is taken here, each without a round.
steps.wait_to_start: No work exists yet: the engine takes this cell's rows for each item that waits, without a round, and the first that takes `ready` gets a work, which starts at the cell that row leads to. Of the items ready, those the owner queued start first, in the owner's order; then the projects with items ready take the free slots in turn, each in its architect's order.
steps.wait_for_start: The agent paused: the engine pauses the work, tells the owner, and waits for the owner's Start; then the work goes back to the cell that paused, in the same session. This pause withdraws a resume that still waits for a free slot, as `resume_work` says. A work on an item that paused for its time budget also has its project's architect look at where it is stuck, as a place to set straight.
steps.bring_up: A work on an older flow version, when it next goes on with no step under way, is brought to the version the engine runs by what it carries now: where it stands, what rows recorded, the returns later cells will read and, in the middle of a cell, the session that cell has open. A new version ends a work only when it has no graph for it (below). The cell it serves is the one it is doing: where it stopped, else the first of the cells that wait for an answer, else the cell it stands at; it has begun that cell once a round ran there since the work last took a row of a cell that is not one of those every agent's cell shares (the tools, the search, the owner's Start, the answers to who interjected) or of the asking part: a round that asked for tools and got their results, or a return sent back, has begun it, and coming to a cell, or standing at an engine's cell that has not run, has not. The returns later cells will read are the newest own answer of each cell the version reads from where the work stands, and the work's last return, which the cell after it reads by where it came from: the cells the work can still come to by the version's rows, from the cell it stands at and the cells it goes back to; each cell those cells read by its id, through an input's place or a database view that names it; and each cell the engine's own code reads by its id. An answer that no cell the work can still come to reads takes no part. An engineer's work whose merge stands (its merge cell took `merged`, and watching main has not taken `broken_by_merge` since) is judged by the rounds after its merge alone: only their returns count, only the cells they walked are gone back to, and only they are done again; its answers from before the merge take no part, later cells reading them as they are, so that neither the engine nor the owner's Start ever takes it back before its merge. Earlier returns of the cells every agent's cell shares and of the asking part are read only so, and are not counted. Each is compared by what its cell takes now, its outcome alone for an agent's, a field taking too what the flow names as it was earlier (`earlier`): absent, or in its shape then, which no return handed in now may be. It moves where it stands, in the same sessions, its version changed and no round recorded, when the version has the graph, every return counted still fits its cell, the cell it stands at is there, the cell it serves (and the agent's cell of the asking part whose session is open: the one it stands at, or the one whose tools are running) has not changed since it began it its kind, its line or the inputs of its own (their names and sources; those every agent's cell has come with what every return shares), and the cells it goes back to are there as cells of the same kind; a session in the middle of a cell is given what the version changed of its format, task and rows, and a return that does not fit them is sent back. Otherwise it comes here, its version changed, with where it goes back to as where it stopped: the first cell of the work's main way whose return does not fit, or the cell it serves when that changed or a cell it goes back to did not hold, or, when the cell it stands at or serves is gone, the latest cell it walked that the version has. It does that cell again from its start: the round it was in is cut off, the question it had out is withdrawn, as the cell that asked does it again, and what it answered, asked and was told stays. A work never goes back past a round that did what cannot be undone: an engineer's merge, once watching main took it back; and what an architect's round does at once: an action on a work or on new starts (a pause, a resume, a start over, new starts held or let go, an interjection), a word to the owner, a message to another project's architect, a change to observations, a reply that went out to an engineer or to the work that reported, and the batch's item changes made after its review. What has not taken effect is done again: the batch's item changes still collected are revised, a reply that waits for the review is dropped, the matters closed whose reply has not gone out go back to the queue, and the notebook is written again. A work that would go back past such a round stays here instead, paused, with the cell as where it stopped, for the owner to decide: the owner's Start takes it there all the same. When the version has none of the cells it walked, it stays here, paused, with nowhere to go back to: once a later flow version that has one is installed, the owner's Start looks again, a paused work not being brought to a new version until it goes on; an engineer's work whose merge does not stand may be started over, or its item cancelled, meanwhile. An engineer's work that stays here asks its project's architect to set it straight, once for each version; an architect's tells the owner alone, by its pause, since the architect it would ask is that work. A work whose graph the version lacks ends, as no cell of the version can run it, and the owner is told why: an architect's work, or a policy setting's of a version before, leaves no hold of its project's new starts for setting it straight, and a policy setting's worktree is removed; an engineer's item gets a new work on the version, at once when a slot is free, else at the head of the queue.
steps.stop_work: A work cancelled, or started over by the owner or its project's architect, which a new work on the version the engine runs takes over, ends here from the cell it stands at, which it keeps as where it stopped. It ends once the step it is in has ended: a cancel or a start over is a request the engine's loop carries out then, and until then the owner's page shows the work stopping; while the engine does not run, the request waits for its next start. A round running when it is asked hands in nothing, and a round still open is cut off. A merge that came first stands, on main or still being made: the work is not cancelled or started over, whoever asked is told, and it goes on to watch main; the engine does not revert it, which is someone's decision. A work taken over leaves its worktree and pull request to the work that takes it over; if the item is cancelled before that work takes them up in its first cell, the cancel removes the worktree and closes the pull request.

actions.answer_architect: Sends the reply to the architect whose message this was, as a message in its queue.
actions.answer_reporter: Tells the work that handed in the matter, a side report or a question, in one line to its engineer that needs no answer, what became of it, so that it does not report it again: the observation recorded or reported once more, or the items that took it in, by number and title; for a side report of which nothing was recorded, why; for a question, only what its reply does not say. At once, or, when the round's item changes say it, once the batch is made; a work that ended is told nothing. For a group, each matter of it is told on its own, from its own way (`with`) and the changes that name it: what became of one is never said to the reporter of another, and a matter with no item change of its own is told at once even when another matter of the group has some. A matter the cell took out of the group (`release_members`) is told nothing.
actions.apply_effects: Carries out the effects of an answer: item changes are collected into the batch for review, a cancel of an item the batch creates cancelling that create out, so that the item is never made and the create, the changes that name its key and the cancel are dropped, saying so; changes to observations, actions and messages to other architects are made at once, and each is logged. A change or a message names the matter of a group it comes of in its `matter`, and is made under that matter's name (an observation's source, an item change's matter); left out, it is the matter picked. A message sent on a matter of flow feedback is marked as flow feedback forwarded, which starts no work of an architect: the architect it goes to takes it in a work that started after it came.
actions.apply_batch: Makes every item change of the batch but those the review drops, as the architect, in one transaction, leaves out with why a change that cannot be made once the review's drops are left out (a dependency that would then close a cycle), logs each with its reason, and those dropped with why, sends the replies and the lines to the works that handed matters in that waited on them, and ends the review's session.
actions.apply_reviewed: Makes the item changes the review found sound, leaves out those it drops and a change that cannot be made once they are left out (a dependency that would then close a cycle), drops those it still finds to fix and logs them with what the review found, puts them to the owner in an ask that holds the matters they came from, sends the replies and the lines to the works that handed in the other matters that waited on them, and ends the review's session.
actions.close_asks: Answers the work's open asks of the owner: no answer is needed, since the work ended.
actions.close_matter: Marks the matter picked as handled by this round, and with it every other matter of its group, if the pick named others to go with it: one round closes them all. A matter the cell took out of the group before (`release_members`) is not among them.
actions.group_picked: Makes the pick's `with` a group led by the matter picked: each matter named is marked as picked with it, so that the cells on the matter's path are given them all and one round of each answers for the group. Before that, any group left unhandled by a work that ended before it was handled falls apart.
actions.dissolve_group: When the cell asks the owner about the matter in hand and it leads a group, the group falls apart: the others are matters of the queue on their own again, to be picked as any other, and the matter in hand alone waits for the owner's answer.
actions.release_members: Takes out of the group each matter the cell's `with` gives the way `back_for_owner`, before the cell's other actions run, so that they find it no longer in the group: it is not closed and its reporter is told nothing, and it is a matter of the queue on its own again, to be picked as any other and to be put to the owner alone when it is taken in. The matter in hand and the others of the group are closed and answered as the cell's other actions say.
actions.close_pr: Closes the work's pull request, when it never merged, saying only that its work ended without merging: why is in the owner's language, and a pull request is in English. A work taken over leaves it to the new work.
actions.deliver_answers: Sends each answer back to the side that interjected: to the owner's conversation, as the agent's message, or to the architect's queue as a report of the kind answer; and records it on the work: those of the answers form, those a redirect carries, and a cell's own answer to the owner's words.
actions.hand_over: Hands the task's blocker on to the holder of the cell the row passes the work on to, recording the move with why and what the holder that hands it on found: to a related project's architect, whose queue gets a matter saying which project and work it is for; the holder handing it on holds nothing then.
actions.hand_over_to_sub_items: Closes the work's draft PR, if any, saying which sub-items took over the work, as the architect's latest reply names them. The work does not merge; it waits for its sub-items.
actions.hold_to_set_straight: Starts no new work of the project while its architect sets it straight; the works running go on.
actions.lock_new_acceptance: Writes the advisor's new acceptance conditions onto the item.
actions.open_session: The line of the cell the row goes to starts a new session there, at the cell's first round in the work: the session manager ends the one the line had going on.
actions.queue_fixes: Queues each place to set straight, or each thing missing, that the plan of what to do next found as a matter of the kind set_straight, picked before others; a running work to pause now is paused at once, as the architect's pause; one that names a matter the queue holds already is not queued again.
actions.queue_flow_feedback: Adds the round's flow feedback, unless it is none, under its cell to the flow feedback of the project's architect: the matter of the kind report that holds it and is not picked yet, or a new one. It starts no work of an architect; a work of the architect takes such a matter only when it came before that work started.
actions.queue_followup: For a report: queues the latest what to do next the work handed in as a matter for the architect, with the report's paths under research/ and the commit the work merged.
actions.queue_for_architect: Queues each side report for the architect once; one that causes harm now (`harm_now`) is due at once, which starts a work of the architect when none runs, and when it comes while a work of the architect runs it is also given to that work at the top of its next round.
actions.queue_slots_free: When slots are free and fewer of a project's items are ready to start than slots are free, queues a matter of the kind slots_free for its architect, with how many slots are free and which items are ready, unless one waits already, new starts of the project are held (by the owner, by the architect, or to set the project straight), the owner has paused every work (none is queued then for any project, whether the owner started its architect or steps it, since no new work can start), the last was handled within the wait the configuration sets (`agents.slots_free_wait`), or the free slots and the items ready are those the last handled held.
actions.raise_blocker: Raises the task's blocker at the cell where its problem arose: an engineer's question, an engine tool's failure, an ask of the owner, a wait for items to deliver or for the owner's ruling, held by the holder of the cell the row leads to. A cell where the work waits raises it with its row that waits, for what it waits for.
actions.record_place: Records where the work runs, and the PR it keeps: every later round runs there, and each push is checked against the last pushed head.
actions.record_tool_runs: Records each run, the pushed head and the PR number under the calling cell.
actions.record_waits: Records the items the architect's reply has this work wait for, as parallel dependencies, since the work already runs. The engineer's session is kept, and the work holds no slot while it waits.
actions.release_straight_hold: New works of the project start again, if they were held to set it straight.
actions.remove_worktree: Removes the work's worktree; its branch stays. A work taken over leaves it to the new work.
actions.replace_design_cards: Marks the work's current decision cards replaced: the owner can no longer rule on them.
actions.reply_to_engineer: Gives the reply to the engineer waiting at its question: at once, or, when the round's item changes are what it says, once the review lets them be made, with the numbers of the items they make; a reply that names an item no change made (the review dropped the change that creates it, the revision left it out, or a cancel in the same batch cancelled it out) does not go out, and its matter goes back to the queue, not handled, with that reply and why, to be answered again.
actions.resolve_blocker: Resolves the task's blocker with what its holder decided and did: the reply, the answer, or the items delivered.
actions.revise_batch: Puts the revised changes in place of the batch's changes, for the review to look at again; a cancel of an item they create cancels that create out, as an answer's effects do.
actions.settle_straight_hold: Releases the hold to set the project straight once every matter that sets it straight is handled and the batch's item changes are made.
actions.tell_owner: Puts each message the return tells the owner in the owner's interface, unread, and notifies the owner; the work goes on, and no answer comes back.
actions.tell_went_back: Tells the owner that the work went back to a cell of the new flow version, naming the round, the versions, the cell and why.
actions.report_stuck: Asks the project's architect, as a place to set straight, about the work that cannot go on in the new flow version, and why: once for each work and version, the same work found stuck again on that version asking nothing more, whether or not the architect handled the matter, and offering a work whose merge stands only the owner's Start once a version with a cell it walked is installed, as its merge refuses a start over and a cancel.
actions.redo_batch: Undoes what the rounds the architect's work goes back to do again did that has not taken effect: the batch's item changes they collected are revised, to be collected again, and the matters they closed whose reply has not gone out go back to the queue, a reply held for the batch's review dropped, to be written again.
actions.wait_on_blocker: Counts the architect's time to act on the task's blocker again from now: the work chose to wait longer.
actions.withdraw_blocker: Withdraws the task's blocker, saying why, and tells its holder: its matter leaves the architect's queue, and its ask of the owner needs no answer.
actions.withdraw_blockers: Withdraws the open blocker of the work that ends, with the end's reason, and tells its holder; a resolution that comes for it later is recorded with it and moves nothing.
actions.withdraw_matters: Withdraws from the architect's queue what the work raised and still waits on it: its questions and its failures, saying why.
actions.reply_to_owner: Puts the reply to the owner's words, as the architect's message, in the conversation the words were said in: the group of the work they were said in, else the owner's one-to-one with the architect; and notifies the owner.
actions.queue_measures: Queues each new measure the signals of the policy that takes effect need, as the approved draft hands them in, as a matter of the kind set_straight, something missing, whose path makes an item that has the engine measure it; a measure the queue holds already is not queued again.
actions.queue_check_policy: Queues the check of whether the policy in force still holds, a matter of the kind check_policy at the head of the queue, with why: what the cell's place given says, or why the cell asks for it. One open already, queued or parked for the owner's reply, stands instead, and takes the why. One asked for with no why of its own, as a new session's understanding asks for it, is not queued while the policy in force and the constitution are those the last check handled had.
actions.queue_make_plan: Queues the plan of what to do next, a matter of the kind make_plan at the head of the queue, after the check of the policy, with why: what the cell's place given says, or why the cell asks for it. One open already stands instead, and takes the why.
actions.ask_approval: Pins the engine's short question to the owner, whether the draft the round wrote is approved (Approve this policy? Reply exactly: approved), in the owner's one-to-one with the architect, as a question of the architect's that parks the matter in hand at the cell, without the draft; the draft is the round's return, which waits for the approval.
actions.queue_group_talk: Queues what was said in the groups of the project's works since its architect last read it, other than to it, as one matter of the kind group_talk, when there is such talk and no such matter is open: the owner's words there, and what the engineers told the owner, which the architect is to know as well. New talk joins the one open, whose material is worked out when it is handled. Like flow feedback, it starts no work of the architect: queued as the architect waits to start, a work picks it only when it came before that work started; queued at the end of a batch, the work that runs takes it.
actions.edit_notebook: Writes each section of the notebook the round rewrote, whole, as the project's architect's notebook's latest version of it; the versions before stay, for the owner to look at.
actions.change_observations: Makes each change to the project's observations a round hands in beside its own answer, at once, as an answer's effects make theirs.
actions.go_on_at_second_cell: Puts the matter in hand back at the head of the queue, to go on at its second cell (`H3` after `H2`, `H5` after `H4`, `P2` after `P1`). The matter that leads a group takes the others with it: they wait in the queue until it is taken again, and its second cell answers for all of them.
actions.write_learned: Adds what the work learned to its item's approach under `Learned:`, with the commits merged.
actions.collect_decisions: Makes each decision the round hands in a change of the batch, of the kind record_decision, from the first matter of the owner's words of the batch it quotes: the engine reads the records it quotes, tells from them who decided and when, takes the words from them as they are and writes the line, which is kept with the change, so that the review reads what is written and the batch writes it once the review finds it sound.
actions.fresh_session: The line of the cell the row goes to starts a new session there, each time the work takes the row: the session manager ends the one the line had going on.
actions.record_acceptance: Writes the acceptance conditions of the plan or the design the work implements onto the item: the research's plan when the work goes straight to implement, the design the owner approved otherwise; later the implementation, a fix or the advisor may change them, saying why. If they are the same as those on the item, nothing changes.
actions.post_design_review: Queues the work's latest design, with what thinking again outside the frame examined, for the project's architect to review at the project's level, as an engineer's question of the kind design_review, which starts a work of the architect when none runs; the matter stands for the work's blocker. One queued already for the same design, not answered nor withdrawn, is not queued again.
actions.ask_owner_review: Puts the work's latest design before the owner, with the architect's comments, as an ask of the owner in the work's group, and notifies the owner: the owner approves it, says what to change, or says to split it along its parts, and chooses an option for each decision point. The ask stands for the work's blocker; one put already for the same comments, not answered, is not put again.
actions.ask_owner_approval: Puts the change before the owner, as an ask of the owner in the work's group with the files the owner approves and the pull request to compare them on, and notifies the owner: reply exactly approved to approve it. The ask stands for the work's blocker; one put already and not answered is not put again.
actions.relay_owner_answer: Gives the owner's answer to the ask of the change, which was not exactly approved, to the work's engineer as the owner's words, which the way on chosen next takes in.

checks.research_only: The worktree is clean, and the commits new in this round touch only `research/`.
checks.measure_matches_runs: An answer of measured has a run of this work's measure tool among the engine's records, a request that was refused not counting; any other answer (not_measured, from_records) has none. Reading the records, with query or otherwise, needs no run of measure.
checks.head_pushed_and_green: The head is the local HEAD, the worktree is clean, it was pushed with ci, and the latest fast CI run on it that ci made is green; so is the latest that ran tests, when a later run ran the lint only, which does not stand for them.
checks.branch_changes_fit_work: Against main, an implementation change has some change, otherwise the agent asks (another PR may have fixed it); a report changes nothing outside `research/`.
checks.conditions_cover_acceptance: There is a row for each acceptance condition (at a re-check, each row names an existing condition); each test named was reported by a run of ci on the pushed head, a name naming a test as the ci tool's tests say, and the tests none reported are named in the next ci, with the tests of the test table, or, when the latest run there could not read its results, run again and taken to the architect if that does not mend it; a project whose configuration names no results of its fast CI is told that no run can report its tests, which is the architect's; the report sections named are in the report.
checks.new_test_results: When the design chose no adversarial testing, or the work goes the light route, which has none: each new-behaviour test this round's test changes add or extend (kind new_behaviour) has two results that match what the latest ci run on the pushed head that reported the test and the latest ci_before run that reported it give for the tests the name names, as the ci tool's tests say: passed is green and failed red; before the change not built is cannot_run, not run is not_run or cannot_run, and results that could not be read are read by running ci_before again; the tests no ci run on the pushed head reported are named in the next ci, with the other tests of the table, or, when the latest run there could not read its results, run again and taken to the architect if that does not mend it; a project whose configuration names no results of its fast CI is told that no run can report its tests, which is the architect's; a test is to be run again when any of the files that ci_before run put on the code before the change changed after it; one red after the change or green before it is fixed in this round.
checks.guard_test_results: When the design chose no adversarial testing, or the work goes the light route, which has none: each old-behaviour test this round's test changes add or extend (kind old_behaviour) has two results that match what the latest ci run on the pushed head that reported the test and the latest ci_before run that reported it give for the tests the name names, as the ci tool's tests say: passed is green and failed red; before the change not built is cannot_run, not run is not_run or cannot_run, and results that could not be read are read by running ci_before again; the tests no ci run on the pushed head reported are named in the next ci, with the other tests of the table, or, when the latest run there could not read its results, run again and taken to the architect if that does not mend it; a project whose configuration names no results of its fast CI is told that no run can report its tests, which is the architect's; a test is to be run again when any of the files that ci_before run put on the code before the change changed after it; one red in either run, or unable to run before the change, is fixed in this round; one not run before the change is the table review's to judge.
checks.adversarial_test_results: Each row's two results match what the latest ci run on the pushed head that reported the test and the latest ci_before run that reported it give for the tests the name names, as the ci tool's tests say: passed is green and failed red; before the change not built is cannot_run, not run is not_run or cannot_run, and results that could not be read are read by running ci_before again; the tests no ci run on the pushed head reported are named in the next ci, with the other tests of the table, or, when the latest run there could not read its results, run again and taken to the architect if that does not mend it; a project whose configuration names no results of its fast CI is told that no run can report its tests, which is the architect's; a test is to be run again when any of the files that ci_before run put on the code before the change changed after it; at a re-check, those red or disputed last time were run again; when tests were written, the head was pushed with ci.
checks.test_kinds_match: Tests the engineer added or extended, which adversarial testing lists as the engineer's, are in the table of the kind the engineer gave in the test changes. A test the adversarial tester wrote whose result before the change does not fit its kind is fixed in this round and run again; one not run before the change is the table review's to judge.
checks.tests_only: The commits from the head the engineer handed over to this head touch only the test paths the project's configuration names.
checks.fact_basis_ran: A basis of fact names a run the engine recorded, and its result is what that run gave.
checks.previous_findings_answered: At the re-check, there is a row for each row the latest fix answered, by its number, and none for another.
checks.table_answered: Every row of the table is answered once, with an answer the table allows for that row.
checks.no_disagreeing_after_insist: A finding the re-check insisted on is not answered disagree again; when neither side gives way, the engineer asks the advisor.
checks.not_caused_by_change: For a red check said not to be caused by the change, the engine checks it itself: the check is red on main as the worktree last fetched it, or in the table of known red checks; a flaky one is answered unrelated_flake. When main's checks cannot be read, it is taken as written.
checks.ruling_matches_advisor: This work did ask the advisor about this row, which ruled or had the architect or the owner rule in its place.
checks.answers_match_speakers: Each answer goes to a side that interjected in this round, one answer per side.
checks.constitution_covered: There is exactly one row for each article of the project's constitution, in the constitution's order.
checks.departure_ruled_by_owner: A reply to an open question that says a design departs from a decision of its item that someone other than the architect made comes only once the owner has answered an ask that holds the question: only whoever made a decision rules on a departure from it. A reply that answers such a question says its ruling in departure (stands or turned_down); a reply to any other matter says none.
checks.policy_text_clean: The policy quotes none of the owner's words; it names no cell of the flow, no item and no date the owner said something.
checks.picked_pickable: The matter picked is one of those that can be picked now. Those picked with it (`with`) are at most 7, each named once, each one that can be picked now, a side report or an engineer's answer, and of the kind of the matter picked: a side report goes with side reports only, an answer with answers only.
checks.group_answered: A group's round answers for every matter of the group, once each, and for none outside it: `with` has an entry for each matter picked with the matter in hand, and none for the matter in hand, one outside the group or one named twice; with nothing picked with it, `with` is left out. At the cell that takes the group in, the matter an observation change, an item change or a message names is in the group too and is not one sent back (`back_for_owner`), and the matter in hand is not given that way.
checks.effects_valid: Every change and action holds: an item named is there, or made by an earlier change of the batch; a key is used once in the batch; an item created has its project (this one), title, problem, why, acceptance, level and deliverable; a split gives each acceptance condition to one new item at most; a dependency made is blocking or parallel; a dependency removed is one the items have then: stored, or made by an earlier change of the batch and not removed or cancelled away since; after the batch's dependencies and moves there is no cycle, counting a dependency a cancel takes away, which stays while a work on the item goes on; an observation's tags are the project's; an observation merged into or closed is open; a merge that makes an observation no item took in yet reported three times or more is folded into an item by a change of the batch, which a change moves ahead, not last, unless that item's work runs; a work paused, resumed or interjected into is running; a message goes to another project's architect; at a cell that answers for one matter, no change or message names another matter; no text of an item holds a line of a decision it did not hold, which only the cell that records decisions writes, and a text that replaces an item's approach keeps every line of the item's decisions, letter for letter, in their order, under their head.
checks.reply_fits_changes: The reply names each sub-item and each item to wait for by its number or by the key a change of this round makes it under.
checks.review_covers_changes: There is exactly one row for each change of the batch, by its number.
checks.changes_valid: The revised changes hold, as effects_valid checks item changes, and each comes from a matter of this batch; each is a change or a decision, one of the two, and a decision holds as the check of decisions says it must.
checks.decision_words_hold: Each decision's records exist and are the project's, each quotation is found letter for letter in the words of its record, which the engine reads again, and none quotes words another decision of the return or its item holds already; the item it names is the project's, a number or the key of an item the batch creates, and one that names none has a title and the project's tags. The architect's quote a matter of the owner's words the batch handled, and the rows that say which matters hold a decision agree with the decisions that quote them; an engineer's name no item, being recorded in the item of its work.
checks.learned_holds_no_decision: No line of the text starts a decision (`Decision (`): a decision is handed in as a decision, from the records it quotes, and the engine makes its line; what is learned holds facts and approaches dropped.
checks.words_all_looked: There is exactly one row for each of the owner's words the batch handled, by their matters; a row that says suggestion has a new observation in the same return.
checks.candidates_known: At most ten candidates, each an open observation of the project.
checks.fix_not_queued_again: A thing missing or a place to set straight that the queue holds already, as a matter not handled of the same kind and the same place or the same items, is not handed in again unless it names that matter in queued; a matter it names so is one the queue holds.
checks.holds_needs_policy: Once the owner replied to the question whether to research a new policy, the check of the policy hands in that it holds only while a policy is in force; with none, it writes the course the project keeps by the reply, or asks again.
checks.policy_or_kept: The writing of the policy hands in the whole policy with a draft written, or, with a draft kept, no policy and no new measures.
checks.notebook_fits: The notebook's sections the round rewrote are each named once, each at most 4,000 characters, and with the sections it leaves as they are at most 12,000 characters in all.
checks.understanding_written: The understanding rewrites the notebook's sections on what the project is now and on what is unclear.
checks.plan_written: The plan rewrites the notebook's plan.
checks.asked_before_writing: The check of the policy hands in write_policy only once the owner said yes to a new policy: by the reply to the question whether to research one, or by the owner's own words, which asked for the check (queued by `H8`'s new_policy).
checks.ask_only_on_open_question: The ways for a question ask the owner only about an open question of an engineer's design, never about an engineer's question, whose engineer waits for the reply; and the question they pin links to the design it is about, as a markdown link to the link the matter holds.
checks.observation_changes_valid: Each change to the observations holds, as effects_valid checks them: a new one has a title at most `items.title_max` wide as the owner's titles are counted (spaces not counted, a character of East Asian wide or full width counting 2, so that a title all in Chinese holds half as many characters; count them before handing it in), says what it is and carries the project's tags; one merged into or closed is open; one a merge makes reported three times is folded into an item moved ahead, as the revised changes say; one an item takes in is folded into it, not closed.
checks.points_chosen: An approved design has one choice for each decision point of the latest design, by its number: none that is no such number, none chosen twice, none left out, and each chosen option one of the point's options.
checks.must_fix_fits_findings: The answer whether anything must be fixed is yes exactly when the first pass or the second found something.
checks.decisions_written: One row for each option the owner chose for a decision point at the review, by its number, none twice, and each file named is one the branch adds or changes under `decisions/` against main.

inputs.free_slots: The free slots, and the machines with room, as each machine's session manager reports.
inputs.project_guide: The project's AGENTS.md, and the index of its records (each file's path and first line), with the full text of the files the item cites.
inputs.local_commits: The bundle of the work's local commits the session manager made (git bundle).
inputs.review_base: What a review reviews, by commits the work's worktree has: main as fetched (`origin/<main>`), which is the pull request's base, the commit of main the branch was cut from or last took main in at, the head under review, the merges of main into the branch since it was cut (an empty list if it never took main in), the git command that reads the change between them, and at a re-review the head the last table review looked at with the merges since it.
inputs.existing_work: What already exists for the item, as pointers to read: its earlier works here, with how far each got, why it ended and the queries that read their rounds, returns, decision cards and asks of the owner, and what each asked the architect and had withdrawn when it ended; where an imported item came from; the branch taken over, with the git commands that show what it adds beyond main; the PR kept, with the gh commands for its description, comments, reviews and checks.
inputs.constitution: The project's constitution, as its configuration names it.
inputs.guide: The project's guide as its main has it: its AGENTS.md, its design goal, and the index of its records.
inputs.cited_nodes: The files of the records the matter at hand names, in full, as the project's main has them.
inputs.since_last_work: What happened in the project since its architect's last work: commits merged on main, works ended or stopped, the CI on main, the owner's words and decision cards ruled, reports that came in; at the architect's first work, the same over the last week. Each list is the latest first, at most 60 of it, then how many earlier ones there are; a commit is given by its message's first sentence, cut at a word to 120 characters.
inputs.board: The project's items running and queued, each with its rank, cell, stage, the route it is marked for and the route its latest work goes (light, normal, or turned to the normal route), what it waits for and who waits for it, each blocking or parallel, what keeps one not running from starting, how long it has run, what it spent and its own pause with who paused it and why, or why its last work stopped; the owner's start queue, the items the owner put first to start, in the owner's order, which start ahead of the ranks, and each item's place in it; the release items with the items under them; dependencies with other projects' items; and, when there are any, the holds on the project's new starts (`starts_held`), each with its reason (owner, architect or set_straight), since when and why, so that the architect sees the owner's hold and does not plan as if new works could start.
inputs.numbers: The numbers the engine measures for the project, each as the architect's work started and earlier, for the trend.
inputs.observations_overview: The project's observations: open per tag, recently recorded or reported again, recently closed.
inputs.observation_tags: The project's set of tags for observations, each with what it covers.
inputs.policy: The policy in force for the project: its direction, why, its principles and the signals that the direction may have to change.
inputs.policy_signals: The signals of the project's policy the engine measures, each with its numbers: a signal that names a measure of the numbers by its name.
inputs.slots: The machines' slots, which every project shares: how many there are, used and free, and how many items are ready; and whether the engine runs works, the owner paused every work, with those that run despite it, or a failed run's cause stops every work.
inputs.queue: The project's queue: the numbers of the matters that can be picked now, and each matter with its kind, item, who waits and since when, and what it is, and for a side report or an engineer's answer an excerpt of its text (its first 400 characters, cut at a word); those held by an ask; whether new starts are held to set things straight.
inputs.batch: The batch so far: the numbers of the matters handled, and each with how it ended; its item changes, those collected so far each whole with the key of an item it creates, made only once the review finds them sound, and those made or dropped; and whether a hold to set things straight was released.
inputs.matter: The matter picked, with its material by its kind, and, for a question whose reply was not sent since an item it named was not made, that reply, the items it named that were made and why each other one was not; for a group, `with` holds each of the other matters of the group in the same way.
inputs.matter_items: The items and works the matter picked concerns, in full; for a group, those of every matter of it.
inputs.item_log: The architect's recent log entries on the item the matter concerns.
inputs.similar_items: The items whose title or problem is close to those at hand, and the works under way whose branches changed the same paths.
inputs.before: What the cell before this one on the matter's path answered of it, as that round handed it in; for a group, its answer for the other matters of the group too, as the same round handed them in (`with`).
inputs.owner_answer: The owner's answer to what was asked about the matter picked, when it comes back with one.
inputs.cross_project: The dependencies between the project's items and other projects' items, each blocking or parallel.
inputs.batch_changes: The item changes of the batch, numbered, each with its reason and the matter it came from.
inputs.changes_touch: The items the batch's changes touch, each in full: as its creator wrote it, its locked acceptance, its rank and level, its dependencies and who waits for it, each blocking or parallel, its decision cards, and its latest work's cell, pull request and what it waits for.
inputs.group_talk: What was said in the groups of the project's works since the architect last read it, at its last reading of it (`H12`), other than to it: the owner's words to the engineers, what the engineers told the owner, and the owner's answers, each with its work and item.
inputs.told_owner: What the project's architect told the owner lately: its latest messages to the owner, each with when and at which cell, oldest first.
inputs.owner_talk: What was said in the project's one-to-one between the owner and its architect since the first round of the architect's previous session (the session of the project's latest understanding that was answered, across the works it ran in): each entry as the owner's page shows it, whole and oldest first, with when, who said it to whom and the words, an ask of the architect's with the owner's answer (counted as made when it was answered, if that was after the session began), and only how many images came with an entry. Before the project's first session there is no lower bound. Over 60,000 characters, the latest whole entries, then one line saying how many earlier ones there are; none when nothing was said since.
inputs.questions: The questions the project's architect put to the owner that wait for the owner's reply, newest first: each question, the cell that asked and when, and the matter it parked.
inputs.notebook_project_now: The text of the section project now of the project's architect's notebook, as the latest round that rewrote it wrote it; none before any did.
inputs.notebook_plan: The text of the section plan of the project's architect's notebook, as the latest round that rewrote it wrote it; none before any did.
inputs.notebook_unclear: The text of the section unclear of the project's architect's notebook, as the latest round that rewrote it wrote it; none before any did.
inputs.notebook_other: The text of the section other of the project's architect's notebook, as the latest round that rewrote it wrote it; none before any did.
inputs.words_behind_changes: The owner's words behind the batch's changes: each matter of the owner's words a change came from, with the words whole, where and when they were said, who the record says spoke them, and what the architect said in that place before them.
inputs.batch_words: The owner's words the batch handled, each by its matter: the words whole, where and when they were said, who the record says spoke them (owner, delegate, or unrecorded) and the parts of them a delegate declared to be the owner's own words (`relayed`), the question they reply to, what the architect said in that place before them, and how the architect handled them: its round, the way on it took and its reply.
inputs.batch_items: The items the batch's owner's words concern, each in full with the lines of the decisions it holds: the item each matter names, the item of the work it was said in, and each item the words or the reply to them name by its number, at most twelve.
inputs.fix_table: The table the work's latest fix answered, as the fix was given it: each row with its number and what it held, a red check with its run and the end of its log.
inputs.new_tests: The engineer's tests of new behaviour with their two results, one row for each: read from the test changes of implementing and fixing (the rows added or extended with the kind new_behaviour), a test written again in a later round having its later row. Nothing is written back to a return.
inputs.guard_tests: The engineer's tests of old behaviour with their two results, one row for each: read from the test changes of implementing and fixing (the rows added or extended with the kind old_behaviour), a test written again in a later round having its later row. Nothing is written back to a return.
inputs.levels: The levels of the installation an item may be at, lowest first, each with its model and what work it is for.
inputs.history_sources: The database's read-only address with the command that reads it, for the gatherer's `sqlite3`; and for its git the directory its own round runs in, a worktree of the project's repository, with the project's main as git has it there (`origin/<main>`).
inputs.main_changes: Before the first round of cells `R1`, `D1` and `I1` each time the work comes to them, the engine merges the latest main into the work's branch when its worktree is clean: the files main changed since the branch last took it, or the files in conflict when it could not merge cleanly, the merge then undone; none when main changed nothing since.
inputs.decisions: The project's decisions in force, as its main has them at the commit the round is pinned to: every file of the directory its configuration names as decisions (decisions unless set) but a README.md, each by its path with its text; none when there are none. A decision a work writes or changes on its own branch is not here until it merges; it is in the work's diff.
inputs.owner_approval: The files of the work's change against main that match a path of the project's `owner_approves`, with the pull request and, for the flow, the flow page that compares it with main; whether the owner approved the work's design at its review, or replied exactly approved to the ask of this change since its last fix; none when the change touches none.
inputs.design_review: The review of the work's latest design: what the architect replied at the project's level, and the owner's answer with the images it sent, as cell `D3` brought them.

values.brought_up: Whether the work brought to the new flow version has a cell there to go back to.
values.came_by: How the work came to choose the way on.
values.cancelled: Whether an item the work's item depended on was cancelled, and the line the work stands on has not taken it up yet.
values.collected_changes: Whether the batch collected item changes before the round that records its decisions.
values.due: Whether a matter in the project's queue is due for its architect, which starts a work of it.
values.entry: How the work came to the understanding question: the architect's first work on the project, or another new session.
values.fixes_before: How many earlier reviews of the batch found something to fix.
values.gates: What the merge gate waits for: the items it depends on while one is not merged, then the owner's approval of a change that touches a path the owner approves.
values.held: Where the question the work put to an architect stands: replied, handed to a related project's architect, waited past its limit of the architect's time, its architect gone, an item the work depended on cancelled, or something said to the line the work stands on
values.interjection: Whether an interjection for the line the work stands on is waiting to be delivered.
values.must_wait: Whether the architect's reply has the work stop now for items not yet merged.
values.next_in_batch: Whether the batch goes on, waits while the owner talks, has the decisions in the owner's words it handled recorded, goes to review, is done, or is done with nothing to rethink: no matter handled and no item changed since the last rethink.
values.report: What kind of report the matter is: one an engineer handed in beside its work, a report's what to do next, an engineer's answer to what the architect said to its work, flow feedback, or a fault of wf-agents forwarded to the architect.
values.route: Where the matter picked goes: the first cell of its kind's path, or the cell that asked when it comes back with the owner's reply, or its second cell when a matter of two cells goes on, the cell of the owner's words when the flow no longer has that cell; a check of the policy back with the owner's reply to its draft takes effect when the reply is exactly approved, and is written again otherwise.
values.split: Whether the reply brought back split off sub-items, and whether this work keeps a part.
values.start: What holds an item back from starting, if anything.
values.turn: Whether the work is first in its project's merge queue.
values.understanding: Whether the session the architect's work goes on in is the one its previous work left, or a new one.
values.waited: Whether every item waited for is merged.
values.work: What the work changes: the implementation, the records only, or a report.
values.decision_points: Whether the work's item carries a decision point.
values.research_rounds: Whether the initial research has run the project's bound of rounds (6 unless `limits.research_rounds` sets it) since it last handed in its answer.
values.merge_failures: Whether this failure in the merge queue is the third in a row since the work last went to the architect for them.
values.review: Where the review of the work's latest design stands: waiting for the architect's comments, for the owner's answer, or answered.

needs.flow_feedback: The project's configuration asks its agents what was wrong with each round's cell (`flow_feedback`, on unless set to false).
